briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. Welcome to the climate briefing for October 1, 2026. Today's climate-related news collected globally highlights the accelerating impacts of climate change and the multifaceted efforts to address them.

sections.title: 🔴 Intensifying Climate Crisis Impacts and Global Warnings
sections.content: Beyond the 'magnitude' of climate change, its 'speed' itself is being highlighted as a serious problem [1]. The world's oceans absorbed a record amount of heat last year, equivalent to 40 times humanity's annual energy consumption, intensifying the sense of crisis [13]. These changes are exacerbating economic damage in regions like North Carolina [63] and worsening coastal flooding during storms on the East Coast [65], demonstrating that U.S. cities are experiencing dangerous coastal flooding [77]. Furthermore, the record-breaking melt of Switzerland's largest glacier is leading to catastrophic ice loss, threatening water supplies [86, 88], and it has been confirmed that climate change is driving up prices for staple food items such as wheat, sugar, and cocoa [73, 80]. Research indicating that the incidence and severity of skin diseases are worsening in connection with climate change in 42% of countries worldwide [6, 70, 74] clearly shows that the climate crisis is already a reality [14].

sections.title: ⚠️ Reality and Challenges of Achieving Carbon Neutrality Goals Domestically and Internationally
sections.content: Domestically, local basic governments are facing the challenge of substantially achieving greenhouse gas reduction targets [14], with some falling short of building and transportation sector goals from the first year of their carbon neutrality plans [15, 21]. Meanwhile, the potential for policy conflicts in the clean energy transition is also emerging, such as the possibility of a 1.3 trillion won fine being imposed during the Korea Rural Community Corporation's solar power expansion efforts [51]. Internationally, a 'regression' has been reported with the omission of climate change education from science standards in Florida public schools [60, 64], and movements hindering climate action are also being observed, such as the spread of misinformation about clean energy in the U.S. [55]. Reports that UK-based banks have provided $8.3 billion to the global coal industry over the past four years, becoming Europe's largest coal financiers [92], and the claim by EDF's CEO that new UK gas and oil projects are 'a given' [90] suggest the need for consistent international efforts to achieve carbon neutrality goals.

sections.title: 🌱 Trends in Renewable Energy Expansion and Innovative Technologies Domestically and Internationally
sections.content: On a positive note, India is accelerating its energy transition by approving a $19.42 billion renewable energy program [48, 94], and global renewable energy company JUWI is simultaneously constructing 1 GW of solar and wind projects worldwide [49]. Domestically, policy changes are being pursued to enhance market efficiency, such as the modification of renewable energy-related systems to preferential pricing and two-way CfD (Contracts for Difference) schemes [45], and the standardization of new renewable energy facility introductions through competitive bidding [47]. Measures have also begun to address the 'grid preemption' issue in offshore wind power generation [50], and the Korea Energy Agency is accelerating efforts by hiring its largest-ever workforce to achieve the 100 GW renewable energy target [46]. Furthermore, various innovative technologies and projects are being explored to overcome renewable energy limitations, including a new technology for 99% removal of ammonia ship emissions [12], the unveiling of a hydrogen innovation blueprint [57], and agricultural water management through reservoir solar power with a 3 GW development target by 2030 [56].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Climate Adaptation and Carbon Neutrality Efforts by Local Communities and Businesses
sections.content: Domestically and internationally, local communities are actively engaged in efforts for climate change adaptation and carbon neutrality. Chuncheon City and Hwasun County are exploring agricultural policy directions to respond to climate change and reviewing agricultural technologies [3, 10]. Samcheok City's Carbon Neutrality Support Center signed an MOU to strengthen the climate adaptation capabilities of climate-vulnerable groups [9, 37]. Gwangmyeong City pledged to create a sustainable and resilient city with its citizens [7]. Numerous local governments, including Yeoju City, Boryeong City, Geoje City, Gimhae City, Seogwipo City, and Incheon Geomdan-gu, are promoting citizen participation by conducting carbon neutrality campaigns, operating experience centers, and implementing daily life practices [23, 26, 27, 29, 31, 32, 34, 35, 36, 41, 43]. Guro-gu is also focusing on nurturing future talent by implementing a 'Carbon Neutral AI Convergence Talent Development' program for elementary school students in areas affected by aircraft noise [17, 38]. In the corporate sector, Kia CEO Song Ho-sung announced plans to accelerate carbon neutrality by applying environmental management across the entire product lifecycle [22, 54], and global accounting firm EY launched an ESG financialization framework to promote green investments by companies [8, 40].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing demonstrates that while the threat of climate change intensifies, diverse domestic and international efforts and innovations to overcome it are continuously underway. International cooperation and local community action will become even more crucial for a sustainable future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
